description:
We are a team passionate about space exploration, astronomy, engineering, and technology. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're building Luned, a lunar mission-planning tool that combines scientific calculations, NASA data, and interactive visualisation to help evaluate landing sites on the Moon.

We're excited to experiment, and turn ambitious ideas into working solutions.

We're looking for: Members with skills in Python, astronomy, physics, data analysis, UI/UX design, 3D visualisation
summary:
At the Moon’s south pole, choosing a landing site is only the beginning. Extreme lighting conditions, rugged terrain, and limited Earth visibility make mission planning a complex challenge. Even a change in landing date can significantly affect a mission’s power and communication opportunities.

LUNED (Lunar Mission Design Studio) is an interactive, data-driven platform that helps users explore lunar landing sites and evaluate mission conditions through an intuitive visual experience.

Using NASA’s SPICE observation-geometry system and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA elevation data, LUNED brings together six connected phases: Discover, Explore, Power, Connect, Plan, and Launch Brief. Users can examine 3D terrain, analyze Sun and Earth positions, estimate solar generation and battery performance, identify potential communication windows, and compare landing sites or mission delays.

Unlike complicated scientific interfaces, LUNED transforms technical calculations into understandable visualizations and a consolidated mission assessment.

Our goal is to make lunar mission analysis more accessible to students, educators, researchers, and early-stage mission planners—helping them explore the engineering decisions behind returning to the Moon.
details:
LUNED — Lunar Mission Design Studio

The Problem

The Moon’s south pole presents unique opportunities for exploration, but also difficult engineering constraints. Its low solar angles, rugged crater rims, and changing Earth visibility complicate decisions about landing locations, mission timing, power systems, and communications.

Although scientific tools exist to calculate planetary geometry and examine lunar terrain, they can be difficult for non-specialists to use. Evaluating multiple sites and dates often requires working across different datasets, programs, and technical interfaces.

Our challenge was to bring these critical mission-planning considerations into one intuitive experience.

Our Solution

LUNED is an interactive, browser-based lunar mission design studio that combines NASA-derived scientific information with immersive 3D visualization.

Instead of presenting users with disconnected calculations, LUNED guides them through six stages of a lunar mission:

01 — Discover: Choose the Destination

Users explore a 3D Moon, select from candidate south-polar landing locations, and configure a landing date and mission duration.

02 — Explore: Understand the Terrain

LUNED visualizes local elevation data derived from NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA). Users inspect the three-dimensional terrain surrounding their selected location and examine its elevation characteristics.

03 — Power: Analyze Sunlight and Energy

Using NASA SPICE-based Sun geometry, the application models changing illumination conditions. Users configure solar-panel area, efficiency, orientation assumptions, battery capacity, and electrical load to estimate energy production, battery performance, and potential power shortfalls.

04 — Connect: Evaluate Earth Visibility

LUNED calculates the changing direction of Earth relative to a lunar site and evaluates geometric direct-to-Earth visibility. Users can examine potential communication windows, loss-of-visibility periods, and the relationship between surface conditions and Earth access.

05 — Plan: Compare Alternatives

This phase allows users to investigate landing delays, compare candidate sites, and search alternative mission dates. It helps demonstrate how mission feasibility depends on both location and time.

06 — Launch Brief: Review the Mission

The final phase consolidates results into a mission assessment covering sunlight availability, Earth visibility, solar energy generation, battery performance, and communication interruptions.

How It Works

LUNED connects a React-based interactive website to a Python scientific backend.

NASA/JPL SPICE kernels provide planetary ephemeris, time-conversion, and body-orientation information. The Python backend uses SpiceyPy to calculate Sun and Earth geometry relative to selected lunar coordinates.

NASA LOLA-derived digital elevation data is processed to generate localized terrain visualizations and support terrain-aware analysis.

The resulting calculations are delivered to the frontend, where users can explore 3D environments, interact with mission timelines, change engineering assumptions, and compare mission scenarios.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, Three.js, and React Three Fiber
  • Scientific backend: Python, SpiceyPy, and NumPy
  • Geospatial processing: Rasterio and PyProj
  • NASA resources: NAIF SPICE kernels and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA elevation data
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code

What Makes LUNED Different?

LUNED is designed around the decision-making process rather than isolated scientific outputs.

Its distinctive features include:

  • An immersive, interactive Moon and local 3D terrain.
  • A unified workflow connecting terrain, lighting, power, and communications.
  • Adjustable engineering parameters with dynamically calculated results.
  • Mission-delay scenarios and comparisons across locations and dates.
  • A consolidated mission assessment showing both opportunities and potential failures.

Importantly, LUNED does not simply declare every scenario successful. Its power and communication models can identify unfavorable conditions, helping users understand why a mission plan may need to change.

Intended Impact

LUNED aims to make lunar mission analysis easier to understand and explore.

For students and educators, it transforms abstract astronomy and engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience. For researchers and early-stage mission designers, it provides a convenient way to investigate candidate conditions and compare preliminary scenarios.

By integrating scientific data into a single accessible interface, LUNED encourages evidence-based exploration and demonstrates how planetary science, software engineering, and mission design can work together.

Limitations and Future Development

LUNED is a research and educational prototype, not flight-certified mission-planning software.

Its power model depends on simplified engineering assumptions, and geometric Earth visibility does not guarantee a functioning communications link. Terrain resolution, time sampling, and model assumptions also affect calculated results.

Future development could incorporate more detailed terrain-horizon validation, higher-fidelity spacecraft power systems, communications link budgets, and expanded site and mission-window analysis.

LUNED turns lunar data into mission insight—helping users move from selecting a destination to understanding what it takes to operate there.
